history.dynasty: Panduvamshi (Somavamsi) of Dakshina Kosala; present structure is a modern reconstruction
history.summary: Gandheshwar Temple is an active Shiva temple on the bank of the Mahanadi River at Sirpur, Mahasamund district, Chhattisgarh. The original temple is dated to the early half of the 8th century CE, from the era of the Sarabhapuriya and Panduvamshi/Somavamsi rulers of Shripura, the capital of Dakshina Kosala. Sources agree the present building is a reconstruction of the much older original and has been heavily renovated and repainted, so its antique character is lost. The courtyard holds ancient sculptures recovered from the ruins - a Buddha in bhumisparsha mudra under a tree, and images of Hara-Parvati, Mahishasuramardini, Vishnu, Chandi and other deities - reflecting Sirpur's shared Shaivite-Buddhist tantric past. Inscriptions in the premises mention the exploits of Mahashivagupta Balarjuna; CONFLICT (verify): one account describes an 8th-century Nagari/Sanskrit slab dedicated to Shiva, another (Wikipedia, citing Stadtner) describes the wall slab as bearing a Brahmi inscription dedicated to Lord Buddha. The temple is the centre of an annual religious fair coinciding with Shivratri. Coordinates are approximate (town-level, verify).

name: Gandheshwar Temple
town_description: Sirpur is a village on the banks of the Mahanadi River in Mahasamund district, Chhattisgarh, about 82 km from Raipur. From the late 6th to the mid 8th century CE it was the capital of Dakshina Kosala under the Sarabhapuriyas and Somavamsis, a major centre of Buddhism and Shaivism alike. Today it is an archaeological site with excavated Buddhist monasteries, Shaivite and Vaishnavite temples, and hosts the annual Sirpur National Dance and Music Festival.
